challenge.method: Compared the publisher plaintext, reference observation and pinned CLI entry point, then ran the fixed reproduction once in fresh scratch. The method staged the complete 2,069-file Git tree, including the imported loader, renderer and writer. Compared the index revision, publisher revision, input representation, recipe, method digest, runtime and measurements. Challenged the write with a preexisting destination, notice substitution parameters and a same-length input mutation.
challenge.results: The fresh run on win32, Windows 11 version 10.0.26300, Python 3.13.5 matched every reference observation field. The text command returned the exact bytes, dry-run returned the same bytes without writing, and add wrote a new 7,048-byte LICENSE with actual SHA-256 a2010f343487d3f7618affe54f789f5487602331c0a8d03f49e9a7c547cf0499. The CLI ran with Python socket events blocked. It refused the preexisting destination and preserved its contents, refused notice substitution parameters, and rejected the same-length altered input. All scoped checks passed. No artifact, representation, method, environment or measurement mismatch appeared.

limitations: The result covers License Index revision 591c4a7021d646e89cedf64e77a36d1dc37870f6, the bundled unchanged recipe, a new scratch destination, omitted notice arguments and the recorded runtime.
The socket guard covered Python socket events in the tested CLI process. Universal network isolation and installer safety fall outside that test.
The replay independently executed the shared pinned method. Both executions share its assumptions, and the replay supplies no independent publisher evidence.
Authority to dedicate a particular work and rights to redistribute it require separate evidence.
